proposals.relationship: Flores identifies Curtin’s Senegambia study as a resource for Braudel’s account of western Africa.
proposals.evidence_note: Flores2008,35/n68 explicitly names Economic Change in Precolonial Africa1975 and attributes a quoted expression to Curtin. This is named scholarly mediation, not fresh reading of either monograph. Flores’s broader criticism of Braudel’s Eurocentric and racial framing remains his own, not automatically Curtin’s position.

proposals.relationship: Murray contrasts Braudel’s capitalist characterization of plantations with Curtin’s limited treatment of their capitalist nature.
proposals.evidence_note: Murray1993,153/n4 gives an explicit comparison of particular works. Undirected; not a claim that Curtin personally replied to Braudel or rejected his entire historiography. Distinct from Braudel’s use of Curtin’s earlier Senegambia work. Braudel1986Englishmanifestation and complete Curtin1990book unread.

proposals.relationship: Murray contrasts Williams’s slavery-capitalism argument with Curtin’s limited denial that the plantation complex directly caused industrialization.
proposals.evidence_note: Murray1993,153/n5 explicitly says Curtin does not directly address Williams beyond that conclusion. Undirected, narrowly scoped comparison; not a general rejection or direct personal reply. Reviewer praises the essays while finding causation and decline less settled. Cited Williams1964edition and Curtin1990book unread.
